question: Find the inverse of $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$ and verify the result by matrix multiplication.
explanation:
Determinant and invertibility
The matrix is upper triangular, so $$|A|=(1)(1)(1)=1\ne0$$ Therefore, its inverse exists.
Proposed inverse
Using the inverse relation, the inverse is obtained as $$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&1\\0&1&-1\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$
Verification by multiplication
Multiplying the matrices, $$AA^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1&1&0\\0&1&1\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&-1&1\\0&1&-1\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$$
Conclusion
Since $AA^{-1}=I$, the stated inverse is verified.
